- Uncovered claim 'The commit was dominated by expansion opportunities.' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts that expansion opportunities dominated the commit (a composition/relative-share assertion about the commit pipeline). No drafted criterion measures the share of expansion within the commit. commit_no_engagement_share is an existing check that can express commit composition of the commit, and it can prove this claim being false (a commit dominated by expansion would fail a check expecting non-expansion dominance). AC3's cycle_length_trend only measures closing speed, not the dominance of expansion in the commit mix. (consider check: commit_no_engagement_share)

- Uncovered claim 'Expansion opportunities were slower to close than projected.' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim is specifically about expansion opportunities' cycle length exceeding projected/expected values. cycle_length_trend measures the trend of average cycle length across all deals, not the differential for expansion opportunities specifically. No drafted criterion isolates expansion cycle length against its projection. The right existing check would be an elasticity_differential-style comparison (expansion vs. baseline cycle vs. projected), which is not drafted. (consider check: cycle_length_trend)

- Uncovered claim 'Committed pipeline overshot reality.' [PARAMETRIC]: This claim is the commit-side oversell (committed pipeline above what closed), which is the same substance as the Q4 forecast-overshoot claim already covered by AC1. AC1's forecast_vs_actual with target_pct 109 measures the forecast being ~9% above actual. The commit overshoot is a distinct metric (commit vs. actual) not separately drafted, and AC1's parameter is calibrated to the 9% forecast gap, not to a commit-specific overshoot. Marking it covered would rely on the assumption that forecast and commit overshoot are identical, which the story does not establish. (consider check: forecast_vs_actual)

[note] Uncovered claim 'The commit was dominated by expansion opportunities.' [PARAMETRIC]: AC2 uses commit_no_engagement_share with min_share_pct=15, which only verifies expansion opportunities constitute at least 15% of commit. The claim's substance is that commit was DOMINATED by expansion (i.e., expansion was the plurality/majority segment, share > 50% or clearly the largest contributor). A share of 15-49% passes AC2 yet contradicts 'dominated.' The check can express the claim but the parameter is far too permissive to fail when the claim is false. (consider check: commit_no_engagement_share)

[note] Uncovered claim 'Expansion opportunities were slower to close than projected.' [PARAMETRIC]: AC3 uses elasticity_differential with min_gap_pp=5, which measures a pricing/closing elasticity gap between segments, not the closing-speed (cycle-length) differential the claim asserts. 'Slower to close than projected' is a temporal/velocity claim best expressed by cycle_length_trend or a realized-vs-projected cycle comparison; elasticity_differential measures a different substance and would not fail when the closing-speed claim is false. (consider check: elasticity_differential)

[note] Uncovered claim 'The gap between what was called and what closed widened through the back half of the year.' [PARAMETRIC]: AC6 uses forecast_vs_actual with target_pct=106, which verifies a single aggregate forecast-overrun magnitude, not a widening trend across the back half of the year. The claim's substance is a directional change over time (gap growing in H2), which no single-point forecast_vs_actual can prove. The check that can express this (a trend check on the forecast-vs-actual gap, e.g. slippage_trend) is absent from the drafted criteria. (consider check: forecast_vs_actual)
